errors.english: Except for the plants that do not grow, all others should be removed.
errors.why: The clause continues 'srog chags' from the previous side: it is the grass in which living creatures have not bred that is in question, not 'plants that do not grow'.

errors.english: The clay materials used for cleaning should be placed in earthenware shards.
errors.why: ལྕི་བ is cow dung, the material for plastering/cleansing, not clay.

fix.find: The clay materials used for cleaning
fix.replace: The cow dung used as plastering material

errors.english: he led them to settle
errors.why: གནས་འཆར་བཅུག means he had them take dependence (niśraya) on him as their teacher, not that he settled them somewhere.

note: Readable Vinaya rendering, but misses the cow-dung detail, the insects clause and the niśraya relationship.

errors.english: With her graceful gait and high, auspicious breasts, the foolish are captivated by the form of a young woman.
errors.why: The passage is a sequence of metrical verses (ending in a four-line śloka) and is rendered throughout as running prose.

errors.english: lacking any limb [note: or part] that does not look upon her faults as virtues
errors.why: The Tibetan says only that they lack any faculty that sees faults; 'as virtues' and the inverted negation are added.

errors.english: They would embrace a woman even if she were covered in sparks from a blazing fire born of iron.
errors.why: This is the hell punishment: the adulterer embraces a blazing iron woman covered in sparks, not a hypothetical 'even if'.

errors.english: those who commit unwholesome deeds through the power of their senses
errors.why: དབང་པོ here goes with the shrieking (loud cries) of evil-doers in hell, not 'the power of their senses'.

note: Gets the drift of the anti-lust discourse but loses the verse form and garbles several images.

errors.english: to counteract the abandonment of non-virtuous phenomena that are incompatible with liberation, such as wrong views,
errors.why: Right view etc. are cultivated as the antidote that abandons wrong views and other unwholesome dharmas, not to counteract their abandonment.

fix.find: to counteract the abandonment of non-virtuous phenomena that are incompatible with liberation, such as wrong views,
fix.replace: as the antidote that abandons non-virtuous phenomena incompatible with liberation, such as wrong views,

errors.english: It is that which is not motivated by views of a noble being, a worldly being, a self,
errors.why: 'Noble, supramundane' qualifies right view itself; it is not a 'noble being' and 'worldly being' in the list of views.

fix.find: It is that which is not motivated by views of a noble being, a worldly being, a self,
fix.replace: The noble, supramundane right view of the noble ones is that which is not motivated by views of a self,

errors.english: that which is prophesied
errors.why: In the list after virtuous and non-virtuous, ལུང་དུ་བསྟན་པ is the ethically determinate (vyākṛta), not prophecy.

note: Generally sound Madhyamaka prose, but the Akṣayamati quotation and the antidote sentence are misconstrued.

errors.english: does not become an object of the path of seeing
errors.why: This quotes the Sāṃkhya verse 'na dṛṣṭipatham ṛcchati': it does not come within the range of sight; it is not the Buddhist darśanamārga.

fix.find: does not become an object of the path of seeing
fix.replace: does not come within the range of sight

errors.english: is the Primal Nature, yet it is also extremely hollow and lacks an intrinsic nature
errors.why: What comes within sight (gardens etc.) is extremely hollow, and so the pradhāna too is hollow; it does not say what is seen 'is the Primal Nature'.

note: Follows the anti-Sāṃkhya argument reasonably but mistakes 'range of sight' for the path of seeing throughout the quoted verse.

errors.english: the ascetic became convinced of his virtues and thought
errors.why: It is the king who becomes convinced of the ascetic's virtues and reflects (he is then addressed as 'Great King').

fix.find: the ascetic became convinced of his virtues and thought
fix.replace: the king became convinced of the ascetic's virtues and thought

note: Verses on anger are well handled; one agent swap in the narrative.

errors.english: the Sangha monastic community must quickly offer assistance and guidance regarding punishments and the like
errors.why: The disciple is to help the preceptor quickly receive the penance etc. from the Saṅgha and be quickly freed; the Saṅgha is not the helper.

fix.find: the Sangha monastic community must quickly offer assistance and guidance regarding punishments and the like
fix.replace: the disciple must help and assist him to quickly receive the penance and the like from the Sangha

errors.english: the resident monk should not merely ask questions; he must also provide
errors.why: The niśraya teacher, except that he need not ask permission, must likewise do these services for the disciple; it is not about 'merely asking questions'.

fix.find: the resident monk should not merely ask questions; he must also provide
fix.replace: the niśraya teacher, apart from not having to ask permission, must likewise provide

errors.english: concealing a remaining offense (shispa) an offense requiring purification
errors.why: ལྷག་མ is a saṅghāvaśeṣa offense; '(shispa)' is not the term.

note: The later list of qualifications is fine, but who does what between preceptor, disciple and Saṅgha is confused at the start.

errors.english: their reversal is the non-existence of non-observation. Therefore, the observation is also called non-existent.
errors.why: Their absence is the non-existence that consists in non-observation, which is why non-observation is itself called 'non-existence'; the English inverts the relation.

note: Dense Pramāṇa commentary rendered mostly accurately, with one muddled sentence on non-observation.
Faithful rendering of the word-by-word commentary on the tigress story.

errors.english: Those who long for the unsurpassed state of enlightenment are possessed of a nature of diligence
errors.why: The four lines are one sentence: the appearance of those like you, who long for the highest state, strive to end harm, are steady and wise, is hard to find; the English splits it into a general statement and a separate claim.

errors.english: you will remember me, who am without worldly existence
errors.why: སྲིད་མེད describes the addressee who has ended existence (cf. སྲིད་མེད་བྱེད་པ above), not the speaker.

errors.english: the Guru of the Gods, the Lord of the Immortals [note: Indra]
errors.why: The guru of the gods (of the Lord of the Immortals, Indra) is Bṛhaspati; the note identifies the guru as Indra.

fix.find: the Guru of the Gods, the Lord of the Immortals [note: Indra]
fix.replace: Bṛhaspati, the Guru of the Gods and of the Lord of the Immortals

note: Covers the side and the narrative close well, but the verses are loosely construed and the Bṛhaspati comparison is mis-glossed.

span_why: The English is a single vague sentence; virtually the entire side (on conceptual cognition, svalakṣaṇa and the replies to the opponent) is untranslated.
note: Not a translation of this side.
